headline: JAZ reports a minimal recursive agent loop matching specialist systems on two bounded workflows
summary: A NeurIPS 2026 TTCL Workshop paper introduces JAZ, whose invoke primitive lets a model generate executable code with recursive model calls while exposing prompt inputs and execution history as variables. In the authors’ three-run StuLife evaluation using GPT-5.4 nano, JAZ reports 69.9% pass rate on 207 far-recall tasks versus 61.8% for Letta (MemGPT), at a reported average cost of $18.30 versus $42.10. On AppWorld self-improvement, it reports 74.2% task-goal completion versus 69.9% for ACE. These are paper-reported benchmark results, not independent replications; the paper documents its protocols and notes baseline implementation differences. The authors’ reproduction repository adds a material version caveat: the published runs used mostly dirty development checkouts, two run commits are no longer available, and the closest installable release is not the literal run version. Its StuLife fork also changed the tool surface and task data for 132 of 1,284 tasks, applying those changes across all five arms.
